extracted.intended_audience: general readers, students, writers, and practitioners interested in comedy and surrealism
extracted.subtask_description: Describes the defining characteristics, techniques, historical precursors, and evaluative theory of surreal/absurdist humour, with examples from literature, theatre, cinema, radio and internet culture. Useful for people studying or creating surreal comedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliberate violations of causal reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Surreal humour is predicated on deliberate violations of causal reasoning, thus producing events and behaviours that are obviously illogical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portrayals tend to involve bizarre juxtapositions, incongruity, non-sequiturs, irrational or absurd situations, and expressions of nonsense. The effect follows from breaking expected cause-and-effect relationships to create humour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of bizarre juxtapositions and non-sequiturs
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ bizarre juxtapositions, incongruity and non-sequiturs to create absurd images and scenarios for humorous effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include Lewis Carroll's hookah-smoking caterpillars or croquet matches using live flamingos; Edward Lear's contradictory statements and odd images. These devices create unexpected mental images that provoke amusement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subversion of audience expectations (build up and knock down)
rubrics_metrics.description: Surreal humour builds up expectations and then knocks them down, emphasising the ridiculousness and unlikeliness of a situation so amusement is founded on unpredictability separate from logical analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set up characters' intentions and then introduce unexpected events that subvert those intentions; the unpredictability, rather than a logical punchline, produces comic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character reaction as a tension-heightening device
rubrics_metrics.description: Either the 'goofball' or the 'straight' character can react with dull surprise, disdain, boredom, or detached interest to heighten comic tension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How characters respond (e.g., deadpan or exaggerated detachment) is an important tool for emphasising the absurdity of events and increasing audience amusement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theatre-specific focus: insensitivity, paradox, absurdity and cruelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Surreal humour in the theatre is usually about the insensitivity, paradox, absurdity, and cruelty of the modern world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage works emphasise social absurdities and can use paradox and cruelty to critique or reflect modern conditions; tone and subject-matter alignment with these themes distinguishes theatrical surreal humour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cinema-specific use of dark humour and shock
rubrics_metrics.description: Absurd and surrealist cinema often deals with elements of dark humour where disturbing or sinister subjects like death, disease, or warfare are treated with amusement and bitterness, creating the appearance of an intention to shock and offend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choosing disturbing subject matter and adopting a mordant, amused attitude can be a deliberate technique to produce surreal comic effects and challenge audience sensibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stretching suspension of disbelief via logical consequence of unlikely premises
rubrics_metrics.description: Surrealist cinema/visual media often stretches suspension of disbelief by logically following the consequences of unlikely, reversed or exaggerated premises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rather than random nonsense alone, a device can be to accept an unlikely premise and then play out its logical consequences to absurd extremes (example: Luis Buñuel, Monty Python). This sustained implication of premises can increase surreal comedy's impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incongruity resolution and the 'absurd image' requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Jokes are seen as nonsensical when they fail to completely resolve incongruities; effective surreal/absurd jokes involve the perception of an appropriate incongruity and often require an additional 'absurd image'—an incongruity of the mental image.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analytical theories (e.g., Rodgers & Pien; Oring) suggest surreal humour often leaves incongruities incompletely resolved, producing an absurd mental image rather than a conventional punchline. Evaluating surreal humour can consider whether the incongruity is perceived as 'appropriate' and whether the absurd image is evocative.
